beats.text: Demons were destroying the prayers of the sages. Every time a sacrifice began, they rained blood and flesh on the sacred fire.
The great sage Vishwamitra came to Ayodhya for help. Dasharatha promised him anything he wished.
'Send Rama with me,' said the sage. Rama was not yet sixteen. Dasharatha was heartbroken, and offered his whole army instead.
But Vasishtha reminded him: a king's word cannot be broken. So Rama and Lakshmana went willingly.
On the road, Vishwamitra taught them the mantras Bala and Atibala, so they would never feel hunger, thirst or tiredness, and then the secrets of divine weapons.
Then came Tataka, a fearsome demoness with the strength of a thousand elephants, who had turned a whole land into a wilderness.
Rama was reluctant to fight her, but the sage reminded him that a protector must protect the innocent. His arrow flew true, and the forest was free again.
